messages.content: what does myself add in i made the picture myself?
it makes clear that you made the picture, rather than someone else making it for you.
can i say i made myself a picture too?
yes, but the order gives a different idea. i made myself a picture can say you made a picture for yourself.
so does myself always do the same work in a sentence?
not always. where it is used helps show whether you mean who did the work or who it was for.
use both in a small example.
i made the picture myself, and i gave it to my sister. i made myself another picture to keep at home.
does the first sentence say my sister helped make it?
no. it says you made it and gave it to her. it does not say she helped.
what if i want to say we both made it?
my sister and i made the picture together.
now ask if she wants to keep it.
would you like to keep the picture we made together?
why not call it my picture in that question?
you can use a different word if it works for your meaning, but we made together keeps clear that both of you helped make it.
can orange be a color and a fruit?
yes. orange can name a color or a kind of fruit. the sentence helps make the meaning clear.
give one sentence for each.
the cup is orange. i ate an orange.
what if i say i saw an orange object?
then orange is the color of the object. the object could be many things. you have not said it is a fruit.
can you know its taste?
no. a color does not tell us whether something is food or what its taste is.
make that explanation shorter.
color alone does not tell us the taste.
now say i have an orange container with fruit inside. is the container a fruit?
no. orange gives the container color there. the fruit is inside it, and the container is a different object.
can the fruit be a different color from the container?
yes. you have not said what color the fruit is.
only give a sentence about an orange cup.
the cup is orange.
write a story about a child reading a sentence that starts with i and asking who that person is. the child should learn that the i in the book is not always the person reading it.

a child opened a story and read i live in a small house near the water. he stopped and told his sister that he did not live near water. she asked who was telling the story inside the book. they read the next few sentences and found that the words came from a boy talking about his own home. the child could say the words while reading without making them facts about his real house. later, he wrote a short story using i for a person he had made up. he told his sister that the story voice was different from his own life, even when he used the same word.
why did he stop after the first sentence?
he thought i might have to mean himself because he was reading the words.
what did the next sentences help him know?
they helped him know who was telling the story in the book.
only give the sentence the child read at the start.
i live in a small house near the water.
if he reads that, does it make the sentence true about his house?
no. he can read words from a story without saying those words are true about his own life.
make that explanation shorter.
reading the sentence does not make it a fact about his real house.
finish with him making clear which part is made up.
he wrote story at the top of his page and told his sister that he had made up the small house. it was not their real home.
i asked about a word i did not know today. i had been reading past it for a while.
what helped you choose to ask this time?
i wanted to understand the whole sentence, not just the parts around it.
you knew which part you needed and asked about that part.
make that reply shorter.
you asked for the part that was not clear.
can you help me write a sentence about it?
i asked about a word i did not know so i could understand the whole sentence.
does that say i understood nothing before asking?
no. it says one word was not clear. you may already have understood many other parts.
now make it about a friend who helped explain it.
i asked a friend about a word i did not know, and their explanation helped me understand the whole sentence.
can you make it shorter?
a friend explained one word, and i understood the whole sentence better.
make that sentence shorter.
understanding that word helped me understand the sentence.
my sister took my book to the library. my brother brought it home. who took the book to the library?
your sister took it to the library.
who brought it home?
your brother brought it home.
can you know my brother took it there too?
no. bringing it home does not say he was the person who first took it there.
now i say he met my sister at the library and she gave him the book.
then the book went with your sister to the library, and your brother got it from her there before bringing it home.
who had it between my sister and me getting it back?
your brother had it between those parts.
can you know he read it?
no. carrying a book does not always mean reading it.
what if i ask whose book it is?
you called it my book, so it is yours from the information you gave.
only give the full journey in one sentence.
your sister took your book to the library, gave it to your brother there, and he brought it home.
my friend asked in a kind way if i could help this afternoon. i cannot. does a kind request mean i should say yes?
no. you can thank them for asking and still say you cannot help. a kind request leaves room for a real answer.
write the reply without a made up reason.
thank you for asking, but i cannot help this afternoon.
can i add i hope you find help?
yes, if you want to. that gives a kind wish without saying you can do the task.
put it together.
thank you for asking, but i cannot help this afternoon. i hope you find the help you need.
what if i can help for only five minutes?
then say that clearly before they plan around more time. i can help for five minutes, but not for the whole afternoon.
can you ask if that much would be useful?
i can help for five minutes. would that be useful, or do you need someone with more time?
why not simply say yes if i have five minutes?
because they may think you can help with more of the task. giving the time helps them choose whether five minutes will help.
make that explanation shorter.
giving the time helps them choose whether five minutes will help.
write a story about a child who sees his drawing moved and first thinks nobody wanted to keep it. he should ask before choosing that reason.

a child came home and found his drawing no longer on the kitchen table. he thought someone had put it away because it was not important. before saying that, he asked his mother where it was. she showed him the page on a shelf, away from the water she had used to clean the table. she had moved it so the water would not reach it. the child looked at the clean table and understood the part he had not seen. he asked her to tell him next time she moved a picture. she said she would try, and he put the drawing back after the table was ready.
what did he know when he first came home?
he knew the drawing was not on the table. he did not know why it had moved.
what reason did his mother give?
she moved it away from the water while cleaning the table.
can you know the drawing was not important to her?
not from what happened. moving it was part of taking care of it in this story.
say that more simply.
we cannot say she did not care about the drawing. she moved it to keep it away from water.
write his request for next time.
please tell me when you move my picture so i know where it is.
finish with him seeing the new place as useful too.
he looked at the shelf and chose to keep another drawing there. the table could be used for meals without putting every picture away each time.
if i understand most of the story, does that mean i understand all of it?
no. most leaves room for parts you do not understand. all would be every part.
make that explanation shorter.
most does not say for sure that every part is clear.
does most leave any question open?
yes. it leaves open whether some parts are not clear.
explain why that can be useful.
someone can ask which parts are not clear instead of giving the whole explanation from the start.
now make a sentence saying i need help with one part.
i understand most of the story, but i need help with this part.
can most still be a useful thing to say?
yes. it can help someone know you do not need the whole story explained from the start. they can ask which part needs help.
only give that question.
which part would you like help with?
now only give the sentence about most again.
i understand most of the story, but i need help with this part.
